Cardiovascular
A medical field or system related to the heart and blood vessels, investigated in this context.

Neurological
A medical field or system related to the nervous system, investigated in this context.

Specialists
Medical experts to whom patients are referred for further investigation.<SEP>Medical professionals to whom patients are referred for investigation.

People
People are advised to be referred to several specialists after investigations.

Vasovagal Syncope
A condition characterized by transient loss of consciousness, commonly referred to as fainting.<SEP>Also known as fainting, this condition accounts for more than 50 per cent of blackouts and may be caused by hot weather, emotion, venepuncture, or more serious causes.

Driving
The act of operating a vehicle, which is the context in which fitness to drive is assessed for individuals with vasovagal syncope.<SEP>The act of operating a vehicle, which individuals should avoid until medical standards are met.

Cardiovascular Conditions Standards
A set of standards used to assess fitness to drive when vasovagal syncope results from non-benign causes.

Person
An individual who is assessed for fitness to hold a specific type of license.<SEP>An individual subject to driving restrictions based on medical history regarding blackouts.<SEP>An individual subject to driving license restrictions based on blackout history.<SEP>An individual whose fitness to drive is being assessed based on medical information and tabulated standards.<SEP>An individual who holds a driver licence and is subject to licensing decisions based on health and driving performance.

Unconditional Licence
A type of license that can be held by individuals meeting certain criteria, which is the subject of the assessment regarding blackouts.<SEP>A driving permit that allows operation without restrictions, which a person is not fit to hold if they have experienced blackouts of undetermined nature.<SEP>A driving license that allows the holder to operate a vehicle without restrictions.<SEP>A driving licence held without conditions, which a person is not fit to hold if they have experienced blackouts that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another condition.

Blackout of Undetermined Nature
A loss of consciousness or awareness where the specific cause cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another known condition.

Conditional Licence
A restricted driving permit that may be considered by the driver licensing authority for individuals with blackout history, subject to annual review and specific criteria.<SEP>A driving license subject to specific conditions and regular reviews.<SEP>A driving licence subject to review by the driver licensing authority, considered for drivers who have experienced blackouts under specific timeframes and medical criteria.

Driver Licensing Authority
The governmental body responsible for evaluating applications for conditional licences based on medical information.<SEP>The governmental body responsible for issuing and reviewing driving licenses.<SEP>The body responsible for granting conditional licences and considering the nature of driving tasks alongside medical conditions.<SEP>The governmental body responsible for issuing and reviewing driving licences based on medical information provided by specialists.<SEP>The entity responsible for issuing, renewing, suspending, or cancelling a person's driver licence, including conditional licences.

Appropriate Specialist
A medical or psychological expert who provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding a person's fitness to drive.<SEP>A medical or psychological expert who provides information regarding a person's fitness to drive.<SEP>A medical professional who provides information to the driver licensing authority regarding a driver's fitness to hold a licence following blackouts.

Syncope
A temporary loss of consciousness caused by reduced blood flow to the brain, which is one of the diagnosable conditions for blackouts.<SEP>A temporary loss of consciousness caused by a drop in blood pressure or heart rate.<SEP>A temporary loss of consciousness due to a lack of blood flow to the brain.

Seizure
A neurological event causing abnormal electrical activity in the brain, which is one of the diagnosable conditions for blackouts.<SEP>An abnormal electrical activity in the brain causing involuntary muscle contractions and loss of consciousness.<SEP>A medical condition characterized by abnormal electrical activity in the brain, serving as a reference point for blackout standards.

Blackout
A sudden loss of consciousness or awareness that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another specific condition.<SEP>A sudden loss of consciousness or awareness that some drivers may attribute to a crash or driving mishap.<SEP>A medical condition causing loss of consciousness that is not covered in existing standards.<SEP>An episode of loss of consciousness that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, seizure, or another specific medical condition.<SEP>A medical event that may occur due to various mechanisms including vasovagal syncope, cardiovascular causes, epileptic seizures, or other factors such as metabolic issues or drug intoxication.

Annual Review
A periodic assessment conducted at least once every year to evaluate a person's fitness to hold a conditional license.

Figure 6
A publication figure detailing the management of blackouts related to driving.<SEP>A visual aid titled 'Management of blackouts and driving' containing information about various medical conditions.

Part A section 2
A section providing general guidance on assessing fitness to drive for medical causes not covered in specific standards.<SEP>A document section providing general guidance on assessing fitness to drive.

data.content:
Table for blackouts of uncertain nature
A reference table used when a blackout cannot be diagnosed as one of the conditions covered elsewhere in the publication.

Cardiovascular and Neurological Investigations
Medical examinations involving the cardiovascular and neurological systems.

Inattention
A state of lack of attention that can cause a driving mishap.

Distraction
An external factor or internal focus issue that can lead to a driving mishap, such as a mobile phone conversation.

Mobile Phone Conversation
A communication activity involving a mobile phone that can serve as a distraction during driving.

Drivers
Some drivers attribute a crash or driving mishap to a blackout to excuse an event caused by other reasons.

Medical standards for licensing
A set of guidelines outlining requirements for unconditional and conditional licences for health professionals.

Health professionals
Individuals in the healthcare field who are required to familiarize themselves with licensing standards.

Unconditional licences
A type of licence where specific conditions regarding driving or other activities are not imposed.

Conditional licences
A type of licence that includes specific conditions, often related to medical history or current status.

Blackouts
Sudden loss of consciousness or awareness, which may occur while driving.

Epilepsy/seizure
A neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, which can cause loss of consciousness.

Hypoglycaemic event
A medical condition resulting from low blood sugar levels, potentially causing confusion or loss of consciousness.

Drug/alcohol misuse
The improper use of medications or alcohol, which can impair driving ability and lead to blackouts.

Section 6.2
A referenced section in the document containing further details on specific topics.

Section 3
A referenced section in the document containing information relevant to blackouts and driving.

Fitness to Drive
The assessment of whether an individual is medically fit to operate a vehicle, based on first principles when specific blackout causes are excluded from standards.

Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Drivers operating commercial vehicles who require a more stringent approach regarding fitness to drive assessments due to blackout risks.

Blackout of Undetermined Mechanism
A medical condition where the mechanism causing a blackout cannot be determined despite extensive investigation.

Fitness to Drive Assessment
A procedure used to evaluate whether an individual is fit to operate a vehicle, specifically when a blackout of undetermined mechanism is present.

Section 1.3 Medical Standards for Licensing
A regulatory document or section containing medical standards used for licensing purposes.

Commercial standards
A set of requirements for drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles, or those requiring a dangerous goods driver licence.

Blackouts of undetermined mechanism
Medical events where the underlying cause cannot be identified.

Conditional licence
A type of driving permit that may be granted to individuals who do not meet standard requirements but are deemed safe by a specialist.

Treating specialist
A medical professional responsible for assessing the safety of drivers with blackouts of undetermined mechanism.

Driver licensing authority
The governmental body responsible for issuing and reviewing driving licences.

Farmer
An individual requiring a commercial vehicle licence for the occasional use of heavy vehicles.

Interstate Multiple Combination Vehicle Driver
A driver operating interstate multiple combination vehicles, whose licence status may differ from that of a farmer.

Examining Health Professional
The health professional responsible for examining persons and advising the driver licensing authority regarding driving conditions.

Patient
An individual with a medical condition who must be made aware of its effects on driving and their legal obligations.

Seizures
A medical condition characterized by recurrent episodes of abnormal electrical activity in the brain.

Epilepsy
A chronic neurological disorder defined by a predisposition to seizures.

Diabetes mellitus
A metabolic disease characterized by high blood sugar levels resulting from defects in insulin production or action.

Vasovagal
A type of seizure or fainting episode caused by a sudden slowing of the heart rate and a drop in blood pressure due to vagus nerve stimulation.

Commercial Standards
Regulatory requirements governing drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger vehicles, or those requiring a dangerous goods driver licence.

Driver Licence
A document or credential that may be conditional, issued by the Driver Licensing Authority after consideration of relevant factors.

Health Professional
An individual who provides details of medical criteria not met, evidence of criteria met, and proposed conditions for a conditional licence.

Medical Criteria
Standards or requirements related to health that must be met or documented when issuing a conditional licence.

Hearing Impairment
A medical condition involving hearing loss that may affect fitness to drive.

Visual Impairment
A medical condition involving vision loss that may affect fitness to drive.

Cognitive Impairment
A medical condition involving cognitive function decline that may affect fitness to drive.

Concurrent Medical Conditions
Multiple medical conditions present simultaneously in a person, which may combine to affect fitness to drive.

Structural Heart Disease
A cardiovascular cause that can lead to syncope.

Arrhythmias
Cardiovascular irregularities that may result in syncope.

Vascular Disease
A cardiovascular condition that can cause syncope.

Epileptic Seizure
A condition accounting for less than 10 per cent of blackouts.

Hypoglycaemia
A metabolic cause of blackouts.

Drug Intoxication
A potential cause of blackouts involving the use or effect of drugs.

Sleep Disorder
A sleep-related condition that may contribute to blackouts.

History
Used in the determination of the mechanism of a blackout based on patient background and symptoms.

Investigations
Medical procedures or tests used to determine the mechanism of a blackout.

Specialist Referral
The process of referring a patient to a specialist for further evaluation when determining the cause of a blackout.
